newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel static with bearish undertone.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel static with bearish undertone.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel oil prices were holding relatively stable, but traders said underlying sentiment was very weak and the market's front end stability was more due to a lack of interest.

"The weakness in crude means there's little chance of moving oil up from the Med which offers some respite for the NWE market, but sellers in the North are having trouble placing product anyway," one trader said.
North Sea low sulphur product was on offer at around $103 fob but buyers were scarce.

In the Mediterranean too straight-run markets were quietly stable with a Tunisian term contract tender thought to have been awarded at around $12-$13 over the mean of high sulphur quotes although this could not be confirmed.
News was also awaited of mid-April Tunisian and end-month Egyptian tenders, the latter is expected to settle at around +7-9 over mean high sulphur quotes.
Traders said there was good availability of Russian high sulphur straight-run cargoes from the Black Sea with some interest for these into the East Med.
Traders said buying interest for most grades was relaxed elsewhere in the Mediterranean.
